checks.name: database_clear
checks.detail: No lock waits: no session is blocked.

audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 315330) sat idle in transaction for 4.1 seconds while holding locks that blocked 12 checkout sessions. Checkout success collapsed from 53% to 19% over 30 seconds, putting $14,993/min of revenue at risk against a 60-second degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian initially requested change-calendar evidence (Invariant I2), which showed no active window covering the workload. After the evidence was supplied, both guardians agreed to terminate. The executor killed the session and verification confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits and 100% checkout success over 10 seconds.
audit.root_cause: The inventory_reconcile batch job (batch_replayable_inventory) opened a transaction and went idle, holding locks that blocked all checkout sessions.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_replayable_inventory workers so idle transactions self-terminate before they can block checkout.
Instrument the inventory_reconcile job to emit a heartbeat or checkpoint marker; its absence would let automation detect a stalled worker seconds earlier.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian acted on complete evidence in Round 1; the Continuity Guardian correctly enforced Invariant I2 but caused a one-round delay by requesting change-calendar data that could have been pre-fetched. No guardian wasted a round or missed evidence once the probe returned.
follow_ups: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 5s for the batch_worker role.
Extend the workload registry to include change-calendar default coverage for each workload class.
Add a liveness probe to inventory_reconcile that alerts if no checkpoint progress is seen for >10s.
